subject: Request: Delete user content vs invoice/usage records retention
messages:
From: Jane Colson <jane.colson@atlashealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@atlashealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data deletion request — are invoices exempt?

Hi Neha —

We received a data deletion request from an end user about their account activity that touches both conversational logs and billing records. The user specifically asks that all "their data" be removed. Before we respond I need clarity on Redwood's stance: if a customer requests deletion of personal data, do you also remove invoices/usage records tied to that user, or are there retention obligations that keep those records for accounting/tax/regulatory purposes?

Key context: Atlas Health keeps invoices for audits and our finance team needs proof-of-usage for billing disputes. The requester is asking commingled deletion (chat history + billing). Please advise whether invoices are actionable to delete and if not, what minimal metadata you retain (e.g., invoice id, amount, dates) and how that is separated from conversational content. Any turnaround time guidance is appreciated — the requester gave us a 30-day window.

Thanks —
Jane Colson
Billing Operations | Atlas Health
[Attachment: invoice-2025-11-17.pdf]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Colson <jane.colson@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion request — are invoices exempt?

Hi Jane —

Short answer: we treat invoice and usage ledger records differently from conversational content. Invoices and the minimal billing metadata required for accounting are retained for compliance and reconciliation. They are not "deleted" in the same way chat logs are, though we can redact certain PII when appropriate. I've looped in Marissa (Finance) and Karthik (Legal/Compliance) to confirm retention windows and any regional constraints.

Couple of practical notes: 1) If Atlas needs a proof package for a past charge we can provide invoice PDFs and hashed usage fingerprints; 2) when a deletion request is submitted via your admin console we will remove conversational payloads and cached payloads as per the policy, but invoices will be flagged and governed by accounts receivable retention.

I'll let Marissa and Karthik confirm specifics (retention periods / exceptions).

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Colson <jane.colson@atlashealth.com>, billing@atlashealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:27:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Data deletion request — are invoices exempt?

Neha / Jane —

Thanks for flagging. From a finance and audit perspective we cannot fully delete invoice records that are required for tax, audit, or dispute resolution. Our standard practice:

- Retain invoice PDFs and transaction-level billing metadata for 7 years in the US (to meet typical accounting and tax retention windows).
- For EU customers, we follow local statutory retention periods which can vary (we document EU-specific terms in the contract appendix).
- When a deletion request targets an individual, we will: 1) delete conversational content and any payloads that are not required for billing; 2) retain minimal billing metadata (invoice id, bill date, amount, billing entity) but we can pseudonymize or hash direct identifiers tied to a person if allowed by local regulations and by mutual agreement.

Operationally: we treat billing records as business records. If Atlas needs redaction beyond our standard process (for example, removing a name from a retained invoice PDF), we will need a formal exception request routed to finance + legal and may require a retention/exception agreement. See attached AR_Invoices_Retention_Guideline.pdf for the standard fields we keep.

If you want, Laura can outline the exact redaction steps and Karthik can advise on legal risk for an exception.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: AR_Invoices_Retention_Guideline.pdf]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Colson <jane.colson@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Data deletion request — are invoices exempt?

Looping off the official legal guidance:

- Invoices and charging records are covered by legitimate interest / legal obligation bases in many jurisdictions (accounting, tax, anti-fraud). That means we cannot unilaterally delete records that would put either party at legal or regulatory risk.
- For personal data deletion under GDPR/CCPA: we can remove or anonymize personal identifiers from billing records where doing so does not prevent Redwood or Atlas from meeting legal obligations. In practice we typically replace customer name/email on retained invoice PDFs with a token and preserve invoice-level metadata (invoice number, dates, amounts) in an auditable ledger.
- Any change to retention beyond the standard policy requires: (a) a joint exception agreement signed by both parties, (b) documented controls for how the data will be handled post-exception, and (c) acceptance of residual risk.

Next steps for Atlas: please confirm whether you want (A) standard deletion response (conversational content removed; billing retained/pseudonymized per policy) or (B) to request a formal retention-exception for full removal of billing material. If option B, your legal team should send the request and we will route internally.

— Karthik
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference
